promo-ww-mistake.title: Your guests are filling in YOUR form #shorts
promo-ww-mistake.description:
Google Forms, a new form: name, attending, number of guests, dietary requirements. Copy the link, put it on the RSVP button in Canva, publish. It works — a guest taps it, fills it in, submits.

Now look where that reply went. My Google Forms, my Responses tab. Google's own help page says it directly: "form owners can download and delete existing responses." I made the form, so I own every reply.

Built it for a friend, or selling it as a template? Every guest list ends up in your account — and the couple cannot see one reply. They need a copy, not a share.

promo-ww-inbox.title: Fifty weddings. One inbox. #shorts
promo-ww-inbox.description:
If it is my own wedding, that is fine — I made the form, so the replies are mine.

If I built it for my sister, every one of her guests is now in my account, and she cannot see a single reply.

And if I sell it as a template, it is worse. Every couple who buys it is sending their guests to my form. Fifty weddings, one inbox.

Sharing the form does not fix it — that only gives them access to mine. The fix is a copy: their own form, owned by them, collecting their own replies.

promo-ww-copy.title: Change one word in the form link #shorts
promo-ww-copy.description:
Selling a wedding website template? A Google Docs Editors community guide describes a neat trick: take the form's address and change the end of it to /copy. Anyone who opens that link is asked to make their own copy — and that copy is theirs to edit.

That is a community guide rather than an official Google page, so test it yourself before you rely on it.

And whichever way you go, put the link on a button rather than relying on an embedded form. Then test it on the published site, on a phone, before a single guest sees it.

📄 Free wedding website checklist: https://geniusjunkie.net/get-wedding-website-checklist/

promo-ww-phone.title: Resize on mobile is not enough #shorts
promo-ww-phone.description:
In Canva's publishing settings there is a switch called Resize on mobile, and Canva's help says it optimises the site for phones and tablets. Turn it on — then do not trust it.

Preview the site in mobile view and go through every page, top to bottom. You are looking for text that has moved, text that has shrunk to nothing, and buttons too small to tap.

Desktop layouts are wide and phones are narrow, so anything placed side by side has to stack — and the stacking is where things go wrong.
